## Preserved failures

The first source version failed `lexlean check` with LLT4001 because three proof modules lacked a direct `R4.Blake3Core` import. Verification did not run. Its separate successor added only those three imports, preserving every semantic JSON payload, but failed source admission again because two calls qualified the current module by name. Verification again did not run. The final successor removes only those two `module` keys from local function references; all other AST nodes, four other proof texts, imports, shared sources, configs and limits are unchanged. Both failed stages, actual diagnostics, independent classifications and source-review misses are retained, with no semantic-negative claim from either failure.

The final unrelated0=0 negative is an actual proof rejection after successful source admission. It is distinct from both LLT4001 failures and from earlier whole-case timeout/OOM failures. Earlier writer/size instruments and invocation RED/GREEN history are preserved separately in the archive. The delivery writer's duration-key mismatch was diagnosed independently before its narrow correction; no native result changed.

## Portable evidence

`results.json` binds each actual outcome review and the archive. `evidence.jsonl.gz` uses the existing exact-evidence JSONL format: one header followed by SHA256-keyed base64 members with all source aliases. It retains all three source versions, all six preparation/invocation evidence roots, exact launchers, both source-admission failures, actual command receipts, genuine locks, reviews, emitted Lean, process records and artifact manifests. Every member and alias was checked against its retained bytes after decompression. The final proof/config files and source manifest remain byte-identical; their original NOT_RUN text is historical preparation status, superseded only by this outcome record.

`artifact-inventory.json` accounts for all255 files across the three positive artifacts. The24 `.olean` binaries remain at their explicit local paths and are hash-inventoried, not committed. The text archive does not claim to contain those binaries. Shared runtime/base source references resolve to the prior committed first-state/case19 archives and fixture, without duplicating runtime implementations.

## Remaining work

This checkpoint does not establish the final published digest, efficiency, an OOM remedy, full Object acceptance, production PrismPM binding or Pages. Outer validation, length, finalization, ROOT and digest encoding remain open. The next bounded source-backed investigation is the first compression and second packed64 full-state certificate from accepted S64, with an intended negative and then the four remaining sibling connections. This needs an independent specification before implementation/native execution; merely carrying an unevaluated compression expression would not certify the literal state or compression.

Seven pending component/model/scenario drafts and the three issue66 files are unchanged. Their concrete obligations remain in the previous first-state checkpoint's archived `pending-model-reconciliation.json`; this result does not promote those claims or waive production `prismpm.lock`, `just vv` or Pages.
